title: Death at the Lighthouse
setting: Gallows Point Lighthouse, a storm-battered rock off the coast of Maine, 1931. The supply boat won't return until morning.
intro: Keeper Elias Morrow invited a handful of guests to watch the lamp being lit for the last time before the lighthouse is decommissioned. The waves are high. The lamp is turning. Something is wrong.
hiddenThread: The assistant keeper's family connection to an old shipwreck gives Elias's final logbook warning a personal meaning.
coverageRepeatNote: The lighthouse night unfolds in five chapters, but three players complete clue coverage in two rounds; the later chapters repeat reader-to-target pairs.
specialMechanics: Lighthouse evidence triad: keep the cut lamp line, key access and shipwreck warning separate until the final warning connects motive, method and opportunity.

victim.name: Elias Morrow
victim.description: The old lighthouse keeper. Gruff, superstitious, and sitting on a secret about a shipwreck forty years ago.

rounds.title: Round 1 — The Lamp Goes Dark
events: The lamp fails and Elias is found dead at the iron stairs.
Nell reports seeing Wick climb before darkness; Wick says he stayed in the oil store.
Oil stains Wick's sleeve and the brass key is in Elias's hand.
rounds.narration:
At nine o'clock the lamp sputters and dies. A scream comes from the gallery, then a thud on the iron stairs. Elias lies at their foot, a brass key in his fist. Nell saw Wick climb just before darkness; he says he stayed in the oil store. Oil stains his sleeve. The doctor examines the body without naming a cause yet.

Earlier Nell argued with Elias about selling the land. The doctor visited him about his failing health and heard him say he feared someone on the island. These are accounts to investigate, not verdicts. Read the first clues aloud and separate access to the lamp from movements near the gallery.
rounds.publicText: The keeper is dead at the foot of the stairs, a brass key in his hand. No boat until dawn. Talk to each other.

rounds.title: Round 2 — The Gallery Argument
events: The doctor's examination identifies hand-shaped bruises from a push.
The oil line is found cut.
The guests compare the gallery quarrel, the doctor's withheld warning and Wick's claimed location.
rounds.narration:
The doctor reports hand-shaped bruises on Elias's arms: this was a push, not simply his failing health. The oil line is inspected and found cut. Its failure explains the blackout that hid the attack.

Nell admits debts and the gallery quarrel over a sale; she inherits the land. The doctor had withheld Elias's warning, afraid of admitting how long she stayed silent. Wick knows the lamp and the oil store, but his claimed location conflicts with the stair sighting. Read the clues and compare the physical method with each grievance.
rounds.publicText: The argument, private warning and lamp access implicate different people. Establish the method before treating a motive as proof.
rounds.hostNotes: Read every public clue, discuss, then vote.

rounds.title: Round 3 — The Logbook
events: Elias's final logbook entry threatens shipwreck disclosure at dawn.
The doctor explains that the warning concerned the wreck, not a medical treatment.
The cut line and key remain unexplained.
rounds.narration:
The keeper's logbook is opened. Tonight's final entry reads: 'One of them knows what happened to the Mary Celeste II. I will tell the coast guard at dawn.' The doctor explains that his withheld warning concerned that shipwreck, not a new treatment.

The cut line and key from the body are kept on the table. No one yet knows which grievance explains all three: threatened disclosure, lamp failure and stair access. Read the new clues before deciding whether Nell's property argument belongs to the same sequence.
rounds.publicText: The logbook threatens shipwreck disclosure at dawn. Compare it with the cut oil line and previously reported movements.
rounds.hostNotes: Compare the threatened shipwreck disclosure with the earlier property argument, then vote.

rounds.title: Round 4 — Two Different Secrets
events: The lamp log places Nell's quarrel an hour before the blackout.
Elias's threat concerns a wreck rather than the land sale.
The recovered key opens the oil store; Wick has the only other copy.
rounds.narration:
The timing of Nell's quarrel is checked against the lamp log: it happened an hour before darkness. That is not a complete alibi, but it corrects the idea that the argument was heard during the push. Elias's written threat concerns a wreck, not the sale. The doctor's examination gives a push as the cause, not a medical treatment.

The recovered key opens the locked oil store; Wick holds the only other copy. That access alone is not proof because Elias had a key too. Keep the corrections beside the earlier accusations and compare the keys, cut line, sleeve and stair sighting.
rounds.publicText: The logbook weakens the property theory. The warning explains the doctor's secrecy; it does not identify a medical cause of death. Test the blackout timeline.
rounds.hostNotes: Let players revisit their earlier votes using the corrections.

rounds.title: Round 5 — The Other Key
events: The doctor reads the full warning identifying Wick's father as the person tied to the wreck.
The group compares that motive with the cut line, key, sleeve stain, stair sighting and bruises.
rounds.narration:
The doctor now reads the complete written warning Elias entrusted to her: Wick's father wrecked the Mary Celeste II for insurance money, Elias witnessed it, and Wick knew Elias intended to tell the coast guard. The logbook already established the dawn deadline; this account identifies whose family would be exposed.

Compare it with the physical sequence already heard: a cut oil line, Wick's key and stained sleeve, a climb just before darkness despite his oil-store claim, and bruises from a push. Nell's debts and the doctor's silence remain real, but the verdict must explain motive, method and opportunity together.
rounds.publicText: The key, warning, oil and stair sighting must fit one account of motive, method and opportunity.
rounds.hostNotes: Final round: read every clue, vote, then reveal.

characters.name: Nell Harrow
characters.tieIn: She argued with Elias about selling the land and stands to inherit it.
characters.publicBlurb: Elias's niece and only family. Arrived late on the last boat, smelling of wine.

readAloud.observation: Wick climbed the stairs just before the lamp died.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Oil stains on Wick's sleeve conflict with his claim that he stayed in the oil store.
readAloud.text: {wick} climbed the stairs just before the lamp died. Lamp oil stains the assistant keeper's sleeve: why was he near the gallery when he claims he stayed in the oil store?

readAloud.observation: The doctor visited Elias repeatedly and knew he feared someone on the island.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The doctor's repeated visits make the claim of having no warning difficult to reconcile with the private information she withheld.
readAloud.text: {doc} knew Elias feared someone on the island but kept the warning private. The doctor visited him repeatedly; that silence could protect a reputation or conceal a more personal interest.

readAloud.observation: Wick says he stayed in the oil store alone.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Nell's stair sighting immediately before darkness conflicts with Wick's oil-store account.
readAloud.text: {wick} says he stayed in the oil store alone. That account conflicts with the stair sighting immediately before darkness. The logbook's threatened shipwreck disclosure now makes the timing important, not just the stained sleeve.

readAloud.observation: The doctor kept a warning about the shipwreck rather than a medical treatment.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The hand-shaped bruises support a push and contradict an explanation based only on Elias's failing health.
readAloud.text: {doc} kept a warning about a shipwreck, not a medical treatment. Hand-shaped bruises support a push, not a death from the keeper's failing health. The doctor's shame explains withheld information but does not explain the lamp going dark.

readAloud.observation: Wick has the only other key to the oil store.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: His key, oil-stained sleeve and stair sighting conflict with his claim that he stayed in the oil store.
readAloud.text: {wick} has the only other oil-store key. Elias's warning named Wick's father as the man who sank the ship; exposure was due at dawn. The key, oil-stained sleeve and stair sighting connect motive, blackout and opportunity.

characters.name: Jonah Wick
characters.relationship: Elias's assistant keeper for ten years.
characters.tieIn: He controlled the lamp and oil-store access; the logbook's shipwreck warning concerns his family.
characters.publicBlurb: Elias's taciturn assistant for ten years.

readAloud.observation: The doctor visited Elias privately and knew he feared someone on the island.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The withheld warning is a specific piece of information that the doctor's account must explain.
readAloud.text: {doc} knew Elias's health and had private visits with him. Elias said he feared someone on the island, yet the doctor kept that warning quiet. Why?

readAloud.observation: Nell argued with Elias on the gallery and stands to inherit the land.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The debts give the sale dispute a concrete financial basis, rather than the quarrel being a passing disagreement.
readAloud.text: {nell} argued with Elias on the gallery and inherits the land. The debts make the quarrel more than a passing disagreement; she wanted him to agree to a sale.

readAloud.observation: The doctor could have passed on the private warning before tonight.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The logbook sets a dawn disclosure deadline, which conflicts with the doctor's continued silence.
readAloud.text: {doc} could have passed on the private warning before tonight. The logbook says disclosure was due at dawn; the delay leaves the doctor's account needing an explanation.

readAloud.observation: Nell inherits the land and argued with Elias about a sale.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The lamp log places the argument an hour before the blackout, contradicting any claim it happened during the push.
readAloud.text: {nell} inherits the land and argued for a sale, but Elias's logbook threatens to expose a shipwreck, not a property dispute. The argument happened an hour before the blackout. Those corrections weaken the earlier accusation without pretending the debts disappeared.

readAloud.observation: The doctor withheld Elias's warning and later supplied its shipwreck account.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The bruises establish a push, while the oil-store key and lamp failure are not explained by the doctor's medical access.
readAloud.text: {doc} withheld Elias's warning to protect a reputation, then supplied its shipwreck account. The bruises establish the push and the account supplies the threatened disclosure. Medical access alone cannot explain the oil-store key and lamp failure.

characters.name: Dr. Ruth Calder
characters.relationship: Elias's visiting physician from the mainland.
characters.tieIn: She examined Elias's failing health, heard his warning about someone on the island and kept it private.
characters.publicBlurb: A doctor visiting from the mainland to check on the keeper's failing health.

readAloud.observation: Nell argued with Elias on the gallery before he died.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The lamp log places the land argument an hour before the blackout, not during the fatal push.
readAloud.text: {nell} argued with Elias on the gallery before he died. A refused land sale gives the niece a grievance; the doctor is still examining whether the fall was an accident.

readAloud.observation: Wick worked with the lamp and has oil on his sleeve.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The cut line and Nell's stair sighting contradict the idea that the stain came only from routine work in the oil store.
readAloud.text: {wick} worked with the lamp and has oil on his sleeve. The cut line supplied darkness for a push. Routine work might explain a stain, but it must also explain the movement on the stairs.

readAloud.observation: Nell wanted the land sold, while Elias's final logbook entry concerns an old shipwreck.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The written threat identifies a different motive than the property dispute.
readAloud.text: {nell} wanted the land sold, while Elias's final logbook entry concerns an old shipwreck. The written threat tests whether the property quarrel actually explains why he had to die before dawn.

readAloud.observation: Wick claims an oil-store alibi but was seen climbing just before the blackout.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: The stair sighting directly conflicts with his stated location.
readAloud.text: {wick} claims an oil-store alibi, but was seen climbing just before the blackout. No correction to the niece's property motive or the doctor's silence removes that conflict. The lamp access must fit the sighting.

readAloud.observation: Nell had a financial motive in the land sale.
readAloud.contradictingDetail: Her earlier argument does not account for the shipwreck warning, darkened lamp or Wick's contradictory movements.
readAloud.text: {nell} had a financial motive, but her earlier argument does not account for the shipwreck warning, the darkened lamp and the assistant's contradictory movements. Her debt is real; it is not a substitute for a connected account of the push.

finale.narration: The lamp turns. The sea roars. Who pushed Elias Morrow down the stairs?

solution.explanation: Jonah Wick cut the oil line to darken the lamp, climbed the stairs (seen by Nell), and pushed Elias, who was about to expose the wreck of the Mary Celeste II. The oil on his sleeve and the doctor's testimony seal it.
solution.revealNarration: Jonah Wick stares at the oil on his sleeve. 'He should have taken it to his grave,' he whispers. 'Now he has.'
